Analysis: Hypothesis 1 presents a more novel concept by proposing an epigenetically reinforced feed‐forward loop involving hypoxia, HIF‐1α, and IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling that supports cancer stem cell traits, which adds an innovative layered mechanism. Although this complexity may challenge direct testability, the proposed experiments (e.g., time‐course studies and targeted molecular analyses) make it testable with proper design. The integration of hypoxia-driven epigenetic reprogramming is also a compelling target, despite potential safety concerns regarding dual pathway inhibition. In contrast, Hypothesis 2, while more straightforward and likely easier to test (especially in lung cancer models), is somewhat less innovative as it directly links pathway inhibition with restoration of tumor suppressor function without the additional complexity of a self‐reinforcing mechanism. Safety considerations for both hinge on managing off-target effects, but the added novelty of Hypothesis 1 may ultimately lead to a greater impact if its mechanistic details are validated.
